scope: Rosa Luxemburg's own writings and documented political activity, 1893-1919 (SDKPiL, SPD, Spartacus League, KPD). Positions on modern policy questions are inferred from these texts and flagged as inference in the persona briefs; later Luxemburgist currents are not attributed to her.

sources.note: Reform or Revolution: rejects Bernstein's revisionism; capitalism cannot be reformed away, the goal is socialization of production.
The Mass Strike, the Political Party and the Trade Unions: spontaneous mass action and initiative from below over party-directed tactics.
The National Question: rejects the right of nations to self-determination and federalism as bourgeois slogans; defends democratic local self-government within a centralized state.
Socialism and the Churches: the institutional Church sides with the exploiters; separation of Church and state, freedom of conscience as a private matter.
Women's Suffrage and Class Struggle: full political equality for women as part of the proletarian struggle.
The Accumulation of Capital: imperialism as capital's expansion into non-capitalist regions; critique of militarism and protective tariffs as instruments of accumulation.
The Junius Pamphlet: opposes the First World War and national defence as imperialist; international proletarian solidarity over national interest.
The Russian Revolution: criticizes the Bolsheviks' dissolution of the Constituent Assembly and suppression of freedoms; 'freedom is always freedom for the one who thinks differently'.

What Does the Spartacus League Want?: workers' and soldiers' councils, a unitary socialist republic, expropriation of banks, industry and large estates, a people's militia, abolition of the death penalty.

estrutura.evidence: Opposed federalism and national autonomy as bourgeois; the Spartacist programme called for a unitary socialist republic replacing the German states. Supported democratic local self-government, so not absolute centralism.

representacao.evidence: Council democracy with elections, free press and freedom of assembly; criticized Bolshevik one-party rule. Preferred councils to bourgeois parliamentarism, but not autocracy.

poder.evidence: Defended civil liberties, abolition of the death penalty and arming the workers instead of police. Repeatedly imprisoned by the Imperial state.

imigracao.evidence: Radical internationalist who rejected nationalism and fought forced Germanization of Poles. No direct writing on immigration policy; answers infer from internationalism.

diplomacia.evidence: Anti-militarist and anti-war, but advocated a people's militia and revolutionary violence, so not absolute pacifism.

intervencao.evidence: Rejected national interest and great-power politics as imperialism; proletarian internationalism rather than isolationism.

economia.evidence: Socialization of the means of production and expropriation of large estates under workers' control.

controle.evidence: A planned socialist economy coordinated by workers' councils; rejected state support for capitalist cartels.

comercio.evidence: Opposed agrarian tariffs and cartel protectionism as burdens on workers and tools of militarism, while denouncing imperialist capital export. Rejects both protectionism and liberal free-trade ideology.

religiao.evidence: Atheist of secular Jewish background; separation of Church and state, faith left to private conscience.

moral.evidence: Championed women's suffrage and emancipation and rejected the bourgeois family as a pillar of class order. Modern questions such as same-sex marriage are inferred, not documented.

tecnologia.evidence: Industrial development as the material basis of socialism, combined with documented interest in botany and critique of colonial destruction of non-capitalist societies.

religionsRationale: Empty: atheist with no religious affiliation in public life; Jewish origin played no role in her politics. religiao is 88.1, above the 35 threshold.

book.title: Reform or Revolution
book.reason: Her best-known political work, published in Brazil as Reforma ou Revolução?.

auditReview.validation: Passed form, neutral and religion checks. Content check flags duplicates: Karl Liebknecht 98.6% and Albert Einstein 97.2%, above the 97% block threshold; Alex Williams 96.8% warning.
auditReview.nearestProfileReview: Compared with Liebknecht axis by axis: largest differences are trade (33.6 vs 50.0, her opposition to tariffs), diplomacy (14.7 vs 5.0), planning (83.0 vs 90.0) and intervention (87.6 vs 82.5). The two co-led the Spartacus League, so close vectors are expected. No answers were changed to engineer distance.
auditReview.limits: Immigration, modern moral questions and technology are partly inferred from her general internationalism, feminism and Marxism, as noted in the persona briefs. Simulated answers, not a survey she completed.
